text:
Bitcoin consolidated within the $62,000–$63,200 range as of Thursday's close, exhibiting structural resilience despite broader geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Sell pressure from Strategy's recent disclosure of offloading 3,588 BTC has been partially offset by anticipation surrounding the Clarity Act in the US Senate, maintaining a defensive buy-wall near the $60,000 mark.

Macro markets registered a slight cooling as the 10-year US Treasury yield snapped its seven-day rising streak to close lower at 4.539%, while the US Dollar Index (DXY) flatlined near 100.95. Despite this brief reprieve in yields, federal funds futures still price in a 65% probability of a September rate hike, keeping traditional assets under pressure. The direct correlation remains intact: high real yields and dollar safe-haven demand continue to act as a mechanical headwind for digital assets, limiting sustained upside momentum until the Fed's terminal rate path is fully defined.
